Renew numbered six-assignment/90-active-minute slices under the continuing authorization; internal cap is not a request for another user approval. Native Sol owner coordinates; bulk implementation and concise independent review use existing OMP OpenCode Go DeepSeek. Check omp --help and exact task schema before dispatch. Start actual implementation promptly rather than repeating historic audits. Saved session paths belong under this phase's sessions directory. No purchases or reset-credit redemption; do not select paid Morph routes for this work. Authenticated Codex Luna is fallback only after an actual Go rate-limit, fresh healthy usage and within existing authorization. No local GPU service or unrelated app/config changes.

Read README.md, FIX_HANDOFF.md, actual catalog, project instructions and git status first. Source each new printed card text from an authoritative printing and record retrieval date before coding it; retain a failing regression for each new rule/mechanic. Preserve existing save/replay digest compatibility and pending-choice/hidden-information boundaries. Read aperture integration/digest and commander-certification references when applicable. Models never implement legality or state-based actions.

Focused affected tests plus one real exact-list four-seat game and separate replay, fmt/build and required CI are the delivery path. Use one concise practical independent review; reuse unchanged evidence, do not recertify every historical matrix. A capped game is capped, never a terminal victory. Existing supported profiles and explicit imports remain exact and playable. Do not silently substitute existing practice decks. Do not claim arbitrary Commander, playing strength, release percentage or ETA.

## Durable handoff / reporting
Attach concrete plan, changed files, sourced cards, exact list snapshots, actual commands/results, reviewed head and unresolved gaps to this SAME card. Native lifecycle tools, not CLI impersonation, for worker heartbeats/comments/review/scheduling. A launch is not completion. Checkpoint before supervisor reserve. # THE APERTURE — a practice slice of Magic: The Gathering

**practice slice / supported card pool / headless 2–4 seats / native 2–4-seat practice / named 20-life and bounded 40-life profiles / NOT Commander**

An original Rust rules engine, a headless CLI, and a native desktop card table.

**FOSS:** original source is licensed **MIT OR Apache-2.0**. See [LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT), [LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE), and the [separate third-party content boundaries](ASSETS.md).

**Working toward graphical Commander v1:** [public GitHub/Pages kanban mirror](https://wulfenbach-jpg.github.io/the-aperture/) (not the internal Hermes board), [roadmap and release gates](docs/ROADMAP.md), [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), and [security reporting](SECURITY.md). Planned support is not current support.

This is a deliberately narrow lab: a small, explicitly implemented card pool with
real rules scheduling (priority, stack, state-based actions, combat), honest deck
import, deterministic replay, and trace-backed coaching. It is not a full Magic
implementation and it says so everywhere it matters.

## What actually works

* **Rules engine** (`crates/core`): typed state, zones and object ids, mana costs
  and payment, London mulligan, priority and stack resolution (consecutive passes
  resolve exactly one stack item), sorcery/instant timing, targets with
  revalidation on resolution, counterspell, scry/surveil pending choices, cleanup
  discard, damage removal, state-based actions, bounded combat with attack/block
  declarations and simultaneous damage, empty-library loss, game win/loss.
* **Supported branch-candidate pool (31 real cards)**: the 16-card practice
  corpus (Island, Mountain, Forest, Grizzly Bears, Runeclaw Bear, Centaur
  Courser, Craw Wurm, Hill Giant, Giant Growth, Shock, Lightning Strike,
  Counterspell, Divination, Opt, Consider, and **Crack the Earth**) plus the
  five sourced command-zone practice cards **Isamaru, Hound of Konda**,
  **Plains**, **Unsummon**, **Time Ebb**, and **Swords to Plowshares**, plus
  the sourced full-combat-prevention instant **Fog** (`{G}`, Oracle: “Prevent
  all combat damage that would be dealt this turn.”), plus the six typed
  activated/triggered-ability practice cards **Prodigal Sorcerer**,
  **Rootwalla**, **Brindle Boar**, **Elvish Visionary**, **Festering Goblin**
  and **Oculus** (see `decks/abilities-practice-a.txt`/`-b.txt`), plus the
  issue-15 effect cards **Mending Hands** (one-shot prevention shield),
  **Angrath's Marauders** (damage-doubling replacement effect for any source
  its controller controls, spells included) and **Wight of Precinct Six**
  (printed “This creature gets +1/+1 for each creature card in your opponents'
  graveyards.” — an additive layer 7c static, not a characteristic-defining
  ability). All three card texts and their printing sources are recorded in
  `crates/core/tests/card_printings.rs`; see
  [docs/issue15-effects.md](docs/issue15-effects.md).
  Isamaru is commander-only and is refused in every ordinary starting library
  because the legend rule is not implemented. Crack the Earth is described here: (`{R}`, Sorcery — Arcane; Oracle: “Each player sacrifices a permanent of their choice.”) from the official Gatherer page recorded in [docs/rules-reference.md](docs/rules-reference.md). The two bundled 40-card practice decks are unchanged and do not contain Crack the Earth. No cards outside this list are supported. This is a branch candidate, not an accepted M1 release.
* **Two bundled 40-card practice decks** (`decks/temur-beats.txt`,
  `decks/izzet-control.txt`).
* **Headless CLI** (`aperture-cli`): `selfplay`, `replay` (verify), `harness`,
  `import`, `import-txt`, `commander-check`, `pool`, `decks`, `coach`,
  `decider-health`.
* **2–4-seat headless candidate (M1, partial and unreleased):** ordered seats,
  turn wraparound/skipping after elimination, all-live priority pass tracking,
  masked per-seat projections, bounded one-defender combat declarations,
  replay v5/save v8 and a `harness` command that runs
  paired 2/3/4-seat seeds and verifies every replay digest. Terminal, capped and
  failed runs are reported separately. The same ordered 2–4-seat engine is now
  exposed by the native table (see the UI bullet below), but this is still
  **not** Commander support. This branch implements
  CR 103.5 starting-player mulligan rounds and one bounded, real fixed-set
  public sacrifice producer (Crack the Earth); independent review and exact-head
  CI remain delivery gates, not an automatic M1 acceptance. Generic APNAP hidden-zone choices,
  dynamic/restarting APNAP and Arcane/splice interactions remain unsupported.
* **Offline Commander profile analysis (#11, analysis only):**
  `aperture-cli commander-check --deck <deck-snapshot.json> --cards
  <cards-snapshot.json> [--json] [--out <report.json>]` validates the
  100-card/singleton profile (with the Basic-Land-supertype exemption), one
  front-face legendary-creature commander, color identity, the basic-land-type
  restriction, recorded ban status, and engine/card support **separately**.
  It is deterministic and offline; snapshots bind their exact embedded bytes
  with SHA-256 provenance. Unknown, incomplete, ambiguous, non-normal or
  unsupported metadata is `not_certified`, never guessed legal; format
  `legal` never means playable. All 2+ commander variants and every non-normal
  layout are refused as `not_certified`. See
  [docs/commander-legality.md](docs/commander-legality.md).
* **Versioned persistence:** replay v5 embeds ordered seat deck snapshots, the
  explicit named profile (`practice-20`, `command-zone-practice-20` or
  `commander-combat-practice-40`), the explicit commander setup (empty for
  ordinary practice), and the recorded first player; save v8 embeds the game,
  replay, seat snapshots, AI settings, the Commander-combat damage ledger and
  digest, including the mulligan round and sacrifice queue. Older replay/save versions are rejected explicitly rather
  than silently reinterpreted, and a recorded `rules_revision` must match this
  build before a replay runs. The pinned rules revision is unchanged.
* **Native desktop UI** (`aperture`): dark charcoal/brass 2–4-seat card table
  with compact 2x2 seat panels, all public battlefields, command zones, life,
  counters, status, stack view, own hand, legal-action buttons, coaching panel
  (category-badged: `[RULE]`, `[SIMPLIFICATION]`, `[STRATEGY]` — see
  `docs/issue19-trace-coach.md`; includes pass-round, response-window and APNAP
  records),
  viewer-masked log, pending-choice controls, one searchable zone inspector,
  an explicitly labelled sandbox with manual table controls, per-seat deck
  import, save/load, undo, text zoom and keyboard navigation. Every model, network and
  file operation runs on a background worker with a visible busy state; the
  frame callback never blocks, and a worker result is applied only while its
  session generation, engine revision, decision serial and seat all still match.
  The human is P0 and every other seat can be driven by the deterministic
  heuristic AI with no model service. The setup controls choose 2/3/4 seats and
  either ordinary 20-life practice or the explicit bounded 40-life
  one-Isamaru-per-seat practice profile; **New game** retains that selection.
  Ordinary defaults use the alternating compiled Temur/Izzet lists. The bounded
  command default uses the compiled command-zone practice library
  (`decks/command-zone-practice.txt`: Plains/Forest/Island plus the supported
  command-zone cards) for every seat, so the supplied white Isamaru is actually
  castable. Explicit `--deck-a`/`--deck-b` and imported lists still replace the
  defaults exactly (or are refused) and are never silently overwritten.
  The renderer uses the engine's masked `PlayerView` for card data, so opponent
  hands and libraries are counts only.
  An accepted action invalidates any in-flight load, so a delayed file read can
  never overwrite the board the player just changed.
* **Tabletop controls, zone inspector and honest sandbox** (UI + core): `Z`
  opens one searchable inspector over every zone this seat may legally see
  (search by name, rules text or cost; filter by seat and zone; a command-zone
  card is never labelled battlefield, and opponent hands and libraries stay
  counts only). `K` opens the sandbox panel: explicit draw, mill, untap, scry
  (keep/bottom), surveil (keep/graveyard), reveal and a +1/+1 counter and life
  editor. Those are **overrides, never legal-match actions**: each one runs
  through one deterministic engine path, emits a typed viewer-masked trace
  event, and taints the session's typed record, which survives save/load and
  makes every result read *SANDBOX-MODIFIED — not a legal match result* (a save
  that carries overrides but claims to be untainted is refused). `Undo (U)`
  rebuilds the position from the deterministic recorded prefix, so the RNG,
  revision and decision serial are exact and nothing the undone action revealed
  survives in the log; it is refused after an override. New game, new table,
  load, branch (both the Study panel button and the `G` shortcut), imported
  start and sandbox reset all require an explicit
  confirmation and report failures in an error state. See
  `docs/issue20-tabletop.md`.
* **Per-seat import / play** (UI): each seat has its own Archidekt URL box, a
  pasted-text fallback and a text-file fallback. Each import is certified on its
  own (name, supported/total counts, practice-profile line, refusal reason);
  **Start imported match (P0 vs P1)** is enabled only when *both* seats are
  certified, applies the exact planned `DeckList` with no substitutions, and
  starts a fresh game/replay that embeds both lists as snapshots. An
  explicitly requested `--deck-a`/`--deck-b` file that is missing or invalid is
  refused loudly — the bundled practice deck is never silently substituted.
* **Deterministic replay**: seed + deck snapshots + accepted actions reproduce the
  same canonical SHA-256 state digest. Save/load round-trips preserve the pending
  choice, the RNG position and the AI mode, and **Set branch / Return to branch**
  rewinds to a labelled study point (the hidden-information boundary is stated in
  the message).
* **Bounded Archidekt import**: `https://archidekt.com/decks/<digits>` (plus the
  canonical `/decks/<digits>/<human_slug>` form, whose slug is ignored) with a
  host allowlist, numeric-id request construction, timeout, size cap, one
  allowlisted redirect maximum, on-disk caching, and strict refusal of anything
  outside the supported pool. Normal single-face cards (provider `layout:
  "normal"`, empty `faces`) are recognized from the top-level `oracleCard`
  metadata; multi-face layouts are refused as not modelled; a quantity that is
  missing, non-integer, zero or above 255 is a clear error rather than a silent
  clamp or skip. A text-list fallback is included.

## Quick start (Windows)

```
launch.cmd            :: builds if needed and starts the native UI
```

or, by hand:

```
cargo run --release -p aperture-ui          # native card table
cargo run --release -p aperture-cli -- pool # what is implemented
cargo run --release -p aperture-cli -- selfplay --seed 1 --verbose
cargo run --release -p aperture-cli -- import --url https://archidekt.com/decks/26206384
```

The CLI and UI both load `decks/*.txt`; the same lists are compiled in, so the
binaries also work from another working directory.

## Packaged, reproducible build

```
scripts\package.cmd
```

Builds a version/commit-stamped, unsigned practice bundle under `dist/` —
`aperture.exe`, `aperture-cli.exe`, the bundled decks, the packaged scope README
and launcher — with a SHA-256 manifest and a `verify-package.cmd` that
re-derives every hash and launches the packaged executable in its smoke mode.
Text payloads and the manifest are deterministic, and the release executables
are byte-identical across repeated builds of the same commit and toolchain.

# FIX_HANDOFF — supervisor acceptance fixes for THE APERTURE

Baseline: commit `265fd19` (109 tests, fmt/clippy/release clean). This round
closes the seven verified acceptance blockers below. Scope was deliberately kept
to those blockers; nothing was rebuilt from scratch, no other repo/config/model
service was touched, and the local Decider-2B service was never restarted.

Evidence for every RED→GREEN cycle: `evidence/supervisor-fixes-tdd.log`.
Runtime reports: `evidence/fix-*.json`, `evidence/screenshots/ui-supervisor-fixes.png`,
`evidence/screenshots/ui-import-refusal.png`.

## Result summary

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --check` | 0 — clean |
| `cargo test --all-targets` | 0 — **134 passed / 0 failed** (was 109; 14 test binaries) |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` | 0 — clean |
| `cargo build --release` | 0 |
| `selfplay --seed 101` | 0 — P0 wins, 452 steps, digest `233431d963e5`, replay verified |
| swapped-deck seeds 11,22,33,44,55,66,77,88 | 0 — 8/8 terminal, replay verified, **P1 6 wins / P0 2 wins** |
| live Archidekt import 26206384 | 0 — 28 unsupported with TRUE reasons (15 multi-face, 13 not-in-pool), launch refused |
| real Decider-2B probe (seed 21, seat 0, 120 steps) | 0 — **13 decider-2b decisions, clean usage, 0 truncation fallbacks** |
| native `--smoke` screenshots | 0 — board + refusal-banner/import-panel captures |

## 1. Archidekt normal cards were falsely unsupported — FIXED

`crates/import/src/lib.rs::classify` rejected every entry with `faces == []`.
A normal single-face card legitimately has `layout: "normal"` and an empty
`faces` array with its metadata (name/layout) on the top-level `oracleCard`.
Now: an entry is only "no provider card data" when the *name* is empty; a
multi-face/meld layout (`faces.len() > 1 || layout != "normal"`) is still
refused as not modelled; otherwise the name is looked up in the pool.

The real deck 26206384 (28 cards) is still unsupported, now with the true
reasons: 15 multi-face (including the two `meld` entries that arrive with empty
`faces`) and 13 ordinary cards "not in the supported pool (15 cards)".

Regression: `crates/import/tests/normal_cards.rs` + a synthetic fixture that
reproduces the real provider shape (`layout: "normal"`, `faces: []`) for a
fully-supported 40-card deck — it now certifies and plans. `normalize_real.rs`
asserts the real reasons (the old "no card data" assertion was provably invalid
and was updated with a comment saying why).

## 2. URL slugs + silent quantity clamping — FIXED

* `parse_deck_url` accepts the canonical `/decks/<digits>/<human_slug>` form
  (and the `/api/decks/…` form) with optional query/fragment; the slug is
  non-authoritative and the request URL is still rebuilt from the numeric id
  against the allowlist. Rejections kept: non-https, non-allowlisted host,
  credentials, ports, `.`/`..`/`%` segments, >1 extra segment.
* `normalize` no longer clamps to `u8` or skips zero: a quantity that is
  missing, non-integer, `0` or `> 255` is a clear `ImportError::Parse` naming
  the value; valid values are retained exactly.

Regressions in `crates/import/tests/url_guard.rs` and `normal_cards.rs`. The old
`'/decks/26206384/extra' is rejected` assertion was invalid under the new (real)
link form and was moved to the accepted list with a comment.

## 3. UI import did not apply a deck — FIXED (vertical path complete)

`crates/ui/src/session.rs` + `app.rs`:

* Two explicit seats (P0 `your seat` / P1 `AI seat`), each with an Archidekt URL
  box, a pasted-text fallback **and** a text-file fallback.
* Each import is certified independently and shows name, supported/total counts,
  the practice-profile line, the refusal reason and the unsupported cards.
* `Start imported match (P0 vs P1)` is enabled **only when both seats are
  certified**. It applies the exact planned `DeckList`s (no substitutions) and
  calls `new_game`, so the engine state and the replay both embed the two lists
  as snapshots and the log/replay restart from revision 0.
* An explicitly requested `--deck-a/--deck-b` file that is missing or invalid is

  replay; an unsupported seat cannot start; text fallback for both seats).

a `std::thread` and returns a proposal, never a mutation. The engine stays
authoritative on the main thread.

  decision serial + seat**; a result is applied only if all four still match.
  Generation is bumped by `invalidate_pending_work` on new game/load/branch
  return/sandbox/import start/settings change — including a new game with the
  SAME seed and digest, which only the generation token can distinguish.

  spinners. `request_load` parses on the worker and applies the snapshot on the
  main thread; a load that completes after the session changed is discarded as

  after the game is over, so an import/health/save/load started on the final

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Capture real Scryfall printing data for the issue-17 starter package.

Usage: python evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py

For every card name below this script performs one `GET /cards/named?exact=...`
lookup and then one `GET /cards/{set}/{collector_number}` lookup for the concrete
printing that the named lookup returned. Requests are paced at 120 ms. The raw
responses, request URLs and retrieval timestamp are written to
evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json; the compact catalog declaration is
written to fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json.

No card data is invented here: every field in the compact declaration is copied
from the Scryfall printing response. Re-running the script re-fetches and
replaces both files (the deck and card snapshots are generated separately by
generate-starter-fixtures.py so their embedded digests stay consistent).
"""

import json
import pathlib
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

UA = "the-aperture-issue17/1.0 (offline supported-corpus fixture capture)"
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

NEW_VANILLA = [
    # white
    "Savannah Lions",
    "Elite Vanguard",
    "Devoted Hero",
    "Eager Cadet",
    "Staunch Shieldmate",
    "Valiant Guard",
    "Yoked Ox",
    "Silvercoat Lion",
    "Glory Seeker",
    "Knight Errant",
    "Oreskos Swiftclaw",
    "Blade of the Sixth Pride",
    "Raptor Companion",
    "Armored Warhorse",
    "Alaborn Trooper",
    "Bastion Enforcer",
    "Loxodon Line Breaker",
    "Pearled Unicorn",
    "Pillarfield Ox",
    "Siege Mastodon",
    "Silent Artisan",
    "Indomitable Ancients",
    "Looming Altisaur",
    # green
    "Norwood Ranger",
    "Willow Elf",
    "Trained Jackal",
    "Balduvian Bears",
    "Bear Cub",
    "Cylian Elf",
    "Kalonian Tusker",
    "Swordwise Centaur",
    "Terrain Elemental",
    "Alpine Grizzly",
    "Nessian Courser",
    "Trained Armodon",
    "Golden Bear",
    "Axebane Beast",
    "Hollowhenge Beast",
    "Durkwood Boars",
    "Feral Krushok",
    "Blanchwood Treefolk",
    "Alpha Tyrranax",
    "Vastwood Gorger",
    "Enormous Baloth",
    # green/white
    "Watchwolf",
    "Armored Wolf-Rider",
    "Grizzled Leotau",
]

EXISTING_NONLAND = [
    "Grizzly Bears",
    "Runeclaw Bear",
    "Centaur Courser",
    "Craw Wurm",
    "Giant Growth",
    "Fog",
    "Swords to Plowshares",
    "Mending Hands",
    "Elvish Visionary",
    "Rootwalla",
    "Brindle Boar",
]

BASICS = ["Plains", "Forest"]
COMMANDER = "Jasmine Boreal"


def get_json(url):
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "application/json"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        return json.load(response)


def main():
    names = [COMMANDER] + NEW_VANILLA + EXISTING_NONLAND + BASICS
    assert len(names) == len(set(names)), "card names must be unique"
    retrieved_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    records = []
    responses = {"retrieved_at": retrieved_at, "cards": {}}
    for index, name in enumerate(names):
        named_url = "https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=" + urllib.parse.quote(name)
        named = get_json(named_url)
        time.sleep(0.12)
        set_code = named["set"]
        number = named["collector_number"]
        printing_url = f"https://api.scryfall.com/cards/{set_code}/{urllib.parse.quote(number)}"
        printing = get_json(printing_url)
        time.sleep(0.12)
        responses["cards"][name] = {
            "named_url": named_url,
            "printing_url": printing_url,
            "named": named,
            "printing": printing,
        }
        for card in (named, printing):
            if card["name"] != name:
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: provider returned {card['name']!r}")
            if card["layout"] != "normal":
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: layout {card['layout']!r} is not normal")
        records.append(
            {
                "name": printing["name"],
                "oracle_id": printing["oracle_id"],
                "scryfall_id": printing["id"],
                "set": set_code,
                "collector_number": number,
                "released_at": printing.get("released_at"),
                "mana_cost": printing.get("mana_cost", ""),
                "type_line": printing["type_line"],
                "power": printing.get("power"),
                "toughness": printing.get("toughness"),
                "oracle_text": printing.get("oracle_text", ""),
                "color_identity": printing["color_identity"],
                "keywords": printing["keywords"],
                "legalities_commander": printing["legalities"]["commander"],
                "named_url": named_url,
                "printing_url": printing_url,
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
            }
        )
        print(f"[{index + 1:02d}/{len(names)}] {name}: {set_code}/{number}")

    records.sort(key=lambda record: record["name"].lower())
    evidence = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json"
    evidence.write_text(
        json.dumps(responses, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    fixture = ROOT / "fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json"
    fixture.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fixture.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "schema": "aperture.starter-sourced-cards.v1",
                "provider": "scryfall",
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
                "note": "Every field is copied from the recorded printing response in evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json. Names/costs/type lines/Oracle text are Wizards of the Coast content.",
                "cards": records,
            },
            indent=1,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"wrote {evidence} and {fixture}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Capture real Scryfall printing data for the issue-17 starter package.

Usage: python evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py

For every card name below this script performs one `GET /cards/named?exact=...`
lookup and then one `GET /cards/{set}/{collector_number}` lookup for the concrete
printing that the named lookup returned. Requests are paced at 120 ms. The raw
responses, request URLs and retrieval timestamp are written to
evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json; the compact catalog declaration is
written to fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json.

No card data is invented here: every field in the compact declaration is copied
from the Scryfall printing response. Re-running the script re-fetches and
replaces both files (the deck and card snapshots are generated separately by
generate-starter-fixtures.py so their embedded digests stay consistent).
"""

import json
import pathlib
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

UA = "the-aperture-issue17/1.0 (offline supported-corpus fixture capture)"
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

    # white

    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "application/json"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        return json.load(response)


def main():
    names = [COMMANDER] + NEW_VANILLA + EXISTING_NONLAND + BASICS
    assert len(names) == len(set(names)), "card names must be unique"
    retrieved_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    records = []
    responses = {"retrieved_at": retrieved_at, "cards": {}}
    for index, name in enumerate(names):
        named_url = "https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=" + urllib.parse.quote(name)

        set_code = named["set"]

        printing_url = f"https://api.scryfall.com/cards/{set_code}/{urllib.parse.quote(number)}"

        time.sleep(0.12)
        responses["cards"][name] = {

            "printing_url": printing_url,
            "named": named,
            "printing": printing,
        }
        for card in (named, printing):
            if card["name"] != name:
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: provider returned {card['name']!r}")
            if card["layout"] != "normal":
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: layout {card['layout']!r} is not normal")
        records.append(
            {
                "name": printing["name"],
                "oracle_id": printing["oracle_id"],
                "scryfall_id": printing["id"],
                "set": set_code,
                "collector_number": number,
                "released_at": printing.get("released_at"),
                "mana_cost": printing.get("mana_cost", ""),
                "type_line": printing["type_line"],
                "power": printing.get("power"),
                "toughness": printing.get("toughness"),
                "oracle_text": printing.get("oracle_text", ""),
                "color_identity": printing["color_identity"],
                "keywords": printing["keywords"],
                "legalities_commander": printing["legalities"]["commander"],
                "named_url": named_url,
                "printing_url": printing_url,
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
            }
        )
        print(f"[{index + 1:02d}/{len(names)}] {name}: {set_code}/{number}")

    records.sort(key=lambda record: record["name"].lower())
    evidence = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json"
    evidence.write_text(
        json.dumps(responses, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    fixture = ROOT / "fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json"
    fixture.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fixture.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "schema": "aperture.starter-sourced-cards.v1",
                "provider": "scryfall",
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
                "note": "Every field is copied from the recorded printing response in evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json. Names/costs/type lines/Oracle text are Wizards of the Coast content.",
                "cards": records,
            },
            indent=1,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"wrote {evidence} and {fixture}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the offline analyzer snapshots for the issue-17 starter package.

Inputs (all real, already captured by source-starter-cards.py):
  evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json
  fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json
  decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt

Outputs:
  fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.deck.json
  fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json
  fixtures/starter-corpus/manifest.json

The snapshots use the existing aperture.commander-deck.v1 /
aperture.card-metadata.v1 schemas. This script only binds bytes; it is not a
legality engine. Certification runs through `aperture-cli commander-check`.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

UA = "the-aperture-issue17/1.0 (offline supported-corpus fixture capture)"
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CORPUS = ROOT / "fixtures/starter-corpus"
DECK_TEXT = ROOT / "decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt"


def sha(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def fetch_bulk_metadata():
    cache = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/scryfall-bulk-data.json"
    if cache.exists():
        return read_json(cache)
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.scryfall.com/bulk-data",
        headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        payload = json.load(response)
    cache.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return payload


def parse_deck_text(text):
    """Mirror DeckList::parse_practice for this exact supported list."""
    entries = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("//") or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        quantity, name = line.split(" ", 1)
        entries.append((name.strip(), int(quantity)))
    return entries


def main():
    responses = read_json(ROOT / "evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json")
    sourced = read_json(CORPUS / "sourced-cards.json")
    by_name = {card["name"]: card for card in sourced["cards"]}
    captured_at = responses["retrieved_at"]
    deck_entries = parse_deck_text(DECK_TEXT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    commander_name = "Jasmine Boreal"
    if commander_name not in by_name:
        raise SystemExit("missing commander source record")
    commander = by_name[commander_name]
    if commander["color_identity"] != ["G", "W"]:
        raise SystemExit("commander identity drifted")

    library = []
    for name, quantity in deck_entries:
        record = by_name.get(name)
        if record is None:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name}: no sourced record")
        library.append(
            {
                "name": record["name"],
                "oracle_id": record["oracle_id"],
                "quantity": quantity,
            }
        )
    raw_deck = json.dumps(
        {
            "commanders": [
                {
                    "name": commander["name"],
                    "oracle_id": commander["oracle_id"],
                    "quantity": 1,
                }
            ],
            "companions": [],
            "excluded": [],
            "library": library,
            "sideboard": [],
        },
        separators=(",", ":"),
        sort_keys=True,
    )
    deck_snapshot = {
        "schema": "aperture.commander-deck.v1",
        "provenance": {
            "kind": "constructed",
            "provider": "the-aperture starter corpus",
            "source": "exact decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt library plus the separately specified commander; identities from the recorded Scryfall printings",
            "captured_at": captured_at,
            "raw_sha256": sha(raw_deck),
            "note": "raw_sha256 covers the exact UTF-8 bytes of raw_deck. This is a constructed singleton starter list, not a captured third-party deck.",
        },
        "raw_deck": raw_deck,
    }
    (CORPUS / "jasmine-vanilla-stompy.deck.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(deck_snapshot, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )

    referenced = [commander_name] + [name for name, _ in deck_entries]
    if len(set(referenced)) != len(referenced):
        raise SystemExit("the fixture deck must name each unique card once")
    missing = [name for name in referenced if name not in responses["cards"]]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"no captured printing for {missing}")
    printings = []
    for name in sorted(referenced, key=str.lower):
        printings.append(responses["cards"][name]["printing"])
    raw_cards = "\n".join(
        json.dumps(card, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True) for card in printings
    ) + "\n"
    cards_sha = sha(raw_cards)
    bulk = fetch_bulk_metadata()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Capture real Scryfall printing data for the issue-17 starter package.

Usage: python evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py

For every card name below this script performs one `GET /cards/named?exact=...`
lookup and then one `GET /cards/{set}/{collector_number}` lookup for the concrete
printing that the named lookup returned. Requests are paced at 120 ms. The raw
responses, request URLs and retrieval timestamp are written to
evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json; the compact catalog declaration is
written to fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json.

No card data is invented here: every field in the compact declaration is copied
from the Scryfall printing response. Re-running the script re-fetches and
replaces both files (the deck and card snapshots are generated separately by
generate-starter-fixtures.py so their embedded digests stay consistent).
"""

import json
import pathlib
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

UA = "the-aperture-issue17/1.0 (offline supported-corpus fixture capture)"
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

NEW_VANILLA = [
    # white
    "Savannah Lions",
    "Elite Vanguard",
    "Devoted Hero",
    "Eager Cadet",
    "Staunch Shieldmate",
    "Valiant Guard",
    "Yoked Ox",
    "Silvercoat Lion",
    "Glory Seeker",
    "Knight Errant",
    "Oreskos Swiftclaw",
    "Blade of the Sixth Pride",
    "Raptor Companion",
    "Armored Warhorse",
    "Alaborn Trooper",
    "Bastion Enforcer",
    "Loxodon Line Breaker",
    "Pearled Unicorn",
    "Pillarfield Ox",
    "Siege Mastodon",
    "Silent Artisan",
    "Indomitable Ancients",
    "Looming Altisaur",
    # green
    "Norwood Ranger",
    "Willow Elf",
    "Trained Jackal",
    "Balduvian Bears",
    "Bear Cub",
    "Cylian Elf",
    "Kalonian Tusker",
    "Swordwise Centaur",
    "Terrain Elemental",
    "Alpine Grizzly",
    "Nessian Courser",
    "Trained Armodon",
    "Golden Bear",
    "Axebane Beast",
    "Hollowhenge Beast",
    "Durkwood Boars",
    "Feral Krushok",
    "Blanchwood Treefolk",
    "Alpha Tyrranax",
    "Vastwood Gorger",
    "Enormous Baloth",
    # green/white
    "Watchwolf",
    "Armored Wolf-Rider",
    "Grizzled Leotau",
]

EXISTING_NONLAND = [
    "Grizzly Bears",
    "Runeclaw Bear",
    "Centaur Courser",
    "Craw Wurm",
    "Giant Growth",
    "Fog",
    "Swords to Plowshares",
    "Mending Hands",
    "Elvish Visionary",
    "Rootwalla",
    "Brindle Boar",
]

BASICS = ["Plains", "Forest"]
COMMANDER = "Jasmine Boreal"


def get_json(url):
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url, headers={"User-Agent": UA, "Accept": "application/json"}
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        return json.load(response)


def main():
    names = [COMMANDER] + NEW_VANILLA + EXISTING_NONLAND + BASICS
    assert len(names) == len(set(names)), "card names must be unique"
    retrieved_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    roles = {}
    for name in NEW_VANILLA:
        roles[name] = "vanilla"
    for name in EXISTING_NONLAND:
        roles[name] = "existing"
    for name in BASICS:
        roles[name] = "basic_land"
    roles[COMMANDER] = "commander"

    records = []
    responses = {"retrieved_at": retrieved_at, "cards": {}}
    for index, name in enumerate(names):
        named_url = "https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=" + urllib.parse.quote(name)
        named = get_json(named_url)
        time.sleep(0.12)
        set_code = named["set"]
        number = named["collector_number"]
        printing_url = f"https://api.scryfall.com/cards/{set_code}/{urllib.parse.quote(number)}"
        printing = get_json(printing_url)
        time.sleep(0.12)
        responses["cards"][name] = {
            "named_url": named_url,
            "printing_url": printing_url,
            "named": named,
            "printing": printing,
        }
        for card in (named, printing):
            if card["name"] != name:
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: provider returned {card['name']!r}")
            if card["layout"] != "normal":
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: layout {card['layout']!r} is not normal")
        records.append(
            {
                "name": printing["name"],
                "role": roles[name],
                "oracle_id": printing["oracle_id"],
                "scryfall_id": printing["id"],
                "set": set_code,
                "collector_number": number,
                "released_at": printing.get("released_at"),
                "mana_cost": printing.get("mana_cost", ""),
                "type_line": printing["type_line"],
                "power": printing.get("power"),
                "toughness": printing.get("toughness"),
                "oracle_text": printing.get("oracle_text", ""),
                "color_identity": printing["color_identity"],
                "keywords": printing["keywords"],
                "legalities_commander": printing["legalities"]["commander"],
                "named_url": named_url,
                "printing_url": printing_url,
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
            }
        )
        print(f"[{index + 1:02d}/{len(names)}] {name}: {set_code}/{number}")

    records.sort(key=lambda record: record["name"].lower())
    evidence = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json"
    evidence.write_text(
        json.dumps(responses, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    fixture = ROOT / "fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json"
    fixture.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fixture.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "schema": "aperture.starter-sourced-cards.v1",
                "provider": "scryfall",
                "retrieved_at": retrieved_at,
                "note": "Every field is copied from the recorded printing response in evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json. Names/costs/type lines/Oracle text are Wizards of the Coast content.",
                "cards": records,
            },
            indent=1,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"wrote {evidence} and {fixture}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

`crates/core/src/catalog.rs` and CLI help edits. The sourced fixtures
(`fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json`, deck snapshot, cards snapshot)

card-support edit.

Command:

```
cargo test -q -p aperture-core --test starter_corpus
```

  panicked at crates\core\tests\starter_corpus.rs:98:32:

every_sourced_vanilla_creature_casts_and_resolves --- FAILED
  panicked at crates\core\tests\starter_corpus.rs:143:41:
  supported vanilla

jasmine_boreal_is_a_typed_supported_commander --- FAILED
  panicked at crates\core\tests\starter_corpus.rs:185:54:

  panicked at crates\core\tests\starter_corpus.rs:215:5:
  line 1: 'Jasmine Boreal' is not in the supported pool

  panicked at crates\core\tests\starter_corpus.rs:46:62:

  panicked at crates\import\tests\starter_corpus_analyzer.rs:74:78:
  deck text: "line 7: 'Savannah Lions' is not in the supported pool"

   frozen legacy lists.

```

# Issue 17 — supported starter corpus

Status: **PARTIAL**. One starter package is implemented and exercised; the
eight-list release gate in the public issue remains open. Only
`jasmine-vanilla-stompy` is supported. Every other entry below is a **planned**
archetype with no exact list and no claimed card support.

The machine-readable target list is
`decks/starter-corpus/manifest.json` (schema `version: 1`). Its `status` field is
`planned`, `implemented` or `certified`; planned entries have `deck_path: null`
because no exact, sourced list has been constructed for them yet.

## Target archetypes

| id | commander | style | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `isamaru-white-aggro` | Isamaru, Hound of Konda | white aggressive one-drop | planned |
| `jasmine-vanilla-stompy` | Jasmine Boreal | green/white vanilla-creature stompy | implemented |
| `talrand-draw-go` | Talrand, Sky Summoner | blue draw-go spells-matter | planned |
| `krenko-goblin-tokens` | Krenko, Mob Boss | red goblin token swarm | planned |
| `ayula-bear-counters` | Ayula, Queen Among Bears | green bear tribal +1/+1 counters | planned |
| `elas-sacrifice` | Elas il-Kor, Sadistic Pilgrim | white/black sacrifice/drain | planned |
| `tatyova-landfall` | Tatyova, Benthic Druid | green/blue landfall value | planned |
| `zada-spells` | Zada, Hedron Grinder | red single-target spell copying | planned |

Isamaru is already an engine-supported commander, but there is no exact
99-card singleton library behind it yet, so its starter stays `planned`.
Talrand, Krenko, Ayula, Elas, Tatyova and Zada are not supported commanders and
are listed in `missing_cards` for their entries.

## First implemented package: jasmine-vanilla-stompy

* Commander: **Jasmine Boreal** — `{3}{G}{W}`, legendary 4/5 Human with no rules
  text. It is a genuine printed vanilla legend and is registered in the typed
  `CardId::SUPPORTED_COMMANDERS` allow-list next to Isamaru.
* Library: **99 cards** in
  `decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt`, commander supplied
  separately:
  * **58 unique nonland cards**, all singleton, all supported: 47 newly sourced
    vanilla green/white creatures, 11 previously supported green/white
    nonland cards (four vanilla creatures, four instants, three creatures with
    already-tested typed abilities);
  * **41 basic lands**: 20 Plains and 21 Forest.
* Total with the commander: 100 cards. No card in the library is legendary, so
  the unimplemented legend rule is never exercised. No nonbasic singleton card
  is duplicated. There is no snow, artifact, enchantment creature, token,
  counter, keyword or unsupported rules text in the package.
* Sourced printings: `fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json` records the
  concrete Scryfall printing, printing URL, Oracle fields and retrieval time for
  every referenced card. Raw provider responses are in
  `evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json`.
* Offline analyzer snapshots: `fixtures/starter-corpus/` contains the
  `aperture.commander-deck.v1` list snapshot, the
  `aperture.card-metadata.v1` card snapshot and a fixture manifest with the
  bound SHA-256 digests. These use the existing `commander-check` analyzer; no
  parallel legality engine was added.

Reproduce the source capture and snapshots:

```
python evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py
python evidence/issue17/generate-starter-fixtures.py
cargo run -p aperture-cli -- commander-check \
  --deck fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.deck.json \
  --cards fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json --json
```

The analyzer reports format legality `legal`, one commander, 99 library cards,
100 total, 61 unique canonical names and engine support `supported`. Its
`gameplay.available` field remains `false` with the pre-existing blanket reasons;
that refusal was deliberately not relaxed. Bounded command-zone and
Commander-combat practice are still **not** the Commander format.

## Phased gaps (why the eight-list gate is open)

1. **Card-support surface.** The implemented pool is 79 cards. Non-vanilla
   archetypes need token creation, activated abilities beyond land mana,
   triggered abilities, keyword semantics, counters as rules objects and
   static/layer effects that this slice does not implement. Those are the
   `missing_interactions` entries in the manifest.
2. **Commanders.** Six target commanders are not in the supported pool.
   Extending the typed registry is deliberately explicit: adding a name to
   `SUPPORTED_COMMANDERS` without implementing its printed text would fake
   support.
3. **Exact lists.** No exact future list is claimed. An entry gets a
   `deck_path` only when a real sourced 99-card library can be constructed from
   supported cards, as Jasmine's was. A 90-land pile or duplicated nonbasic
   singleton cards would not be a meaningful style and is not used to satisfy
   counts.
4. **Certification.** `implemented` means an exact list exists, is analyzer
   legal/supported and has played an exact four-seat bounded game. It does not
   mean eight-list certification, independent review or merged CI.

## Exclusion policy

* Only cards whose complete printed text maps to implemented engine semantics
  may enter the catalog. Unsupported text means the card is refused, never
  approximated.
* Genuine vanilla creatures are preferred for volume: they add no hidden
  keyword, token, counter or replacement semantics.
* Legendary cards are commander-only. The legend rule is not modelled, so a
  supported commander is refused in ordinary starting libraries and no other
  legend may enter a starter library.
* Nonbasic singleton cards may appear once per list. Basic lands are the only
  repeatable cards.
* Source data must come from an authoritative printing (Scryfall printing
  endpoint or official Gatherer) with a retrieval date. No card name, cost,
  type line, power/toughness or Oracle text is authored by hand.
* Format legality, engine support and actual gameplay support are reported
  separately. A legal/supported list is still not Commander format gameplay.

## Practical limitations

* The game/replay journey is a local 2–4-seat deterministic heuristic run under
  the explicit bounded 40-life Commander-combat practice profile; it is not
  networked multiplayer or full Commander.
* The AI is the existing deterministic heuristic. This package adds no
  strategy tuning.
* The native UI's bundled table still defaults to the practice decks; the
  starter corpus is exercised through the CLI with explicit deck paths.

# Issue 15 — replacement, prevention and layered continuous effects

Rules citation: Comprehensive Rules revision pinned by `RULES_REVISION`
(2026-09-25). Everything below is the typed rules layer; no UI or AI code decides
these outcomes.

## Card text provenance

Every card this lane added to the pool is implemented from a printing, not from
hand-authored wording. The records (set, collector number, Scryfall URI,
retrieval date, how many printings were checked, and the exact oracle text and
P/T) live in `crates/core/tests/card_printings.rs`; the test
`every_new_pool_card_matches_its_recorded_authoritative_printing` fails if the
catalog string ever drifts from them, and
`every_pool_card_added_after_issue_15_has_a_recorded_printing` fails when a card
is added to the pool without a record — so the next hand-authored oracle string

# Issue 20 — tabletop-grade controls, one searchable zone inspector, honest sandbox

This is bounded 28–31-card practice on the real native four-seat table, not
Commander, not a trainer and not v1. It adds the manual table furniture a player
needs while practising: one searchable zone inspector, explicit table controls,
an explicitly labelled sandbox that taints the session, an honest undo, and
confirmations for every destructive action.

## 1. One searchable zone inspector

`Z` opens **Zone inspector — searchable, viewer-masked**. It is built from the
engine's masked `PlayerView` for the human seat and from nothing else:

* search matches name, printed rules text or mana cost, case-insensitively;
* filters narrow by seat (P0..P3) and by zone (hand, battlefield, graveyard,
  exile, command);
* every seat's counts are listed, and each count is a button that filters the
  inspector to that seat and zone;
* a card's zone comes from `PlayerView::zone_of`, so the shared inspector never
  hardcodes a location: a command-zone card reports `command zone`, and a card
  that is not projected at all reports *no* zone instead of inventing one;
* opponent hands and every library are counts only. They cannot match, and the
  inspector says so rather than showing an unexplained empty list.

`docs/issue18-native-table.md` remains the reference for the four-seat layout and
the fixed primary strip. The window minimum eframe actually enforces is
**1024×640** (`crates/ui/src/main.rs`); 1280×720 is the acceptance viewport. Both
sizes are exercised against `render_ui` for the inspector, the sandbox panel and
the primary strip — the inspector is a floating window and does not change the
persistent strip at either size.

## 2. Manual table controls (all sandbox overrides)

Open the sandbox panel with `K`. Every control there is an **override**, never a
legal-match action. Each one:

* runs through one deterministic engine path (`Game::sandbox`) with no random
  draws, so it cannot disturb the RNG position;
* emits exactly one typed, viewer-aware `Event::SandboxOverride` trace event;
* bumps the engine revision and decision serial, so an outstanding submission
  or a background AI decision computed against the old position is stale;
* is refused with a reason while a rules choice is pending, mid-resolution, on
  an empty or too-small library, or when a commander is on top of the library
  (its CR 903.9b zone-change choice is a rules decision, not an override).

| control | effect | visibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draw 1 | top of your library to your hand | your draw is yours; opponents see "draws a card" |
| Mill 1 | top card to your graveyard, no dies trigger (CR 701.13a) | public (graveyard) |
| Untap all | untap your permanents; **not** an untap step, so summoning sickness is unchanged (CR 502) | public |
| Scry 1 · keep on top / to bottom | look at the top card; keep it or put it on the bottom in the same order (CR 701.22a) | the look is private to your seat |
| Surveil 1 · keep on top / to graveyard | look at the top card; keep it or put it into the graveyard (CR 701.25a) | the look is private to your seat |
| Reveal top 3 | show the top three cards to every seat | public by construction |
| Counter editor | set / add / clear +1/+1 counters on one of your permanents (0..=99) | public; **storage and display only** — this engine's combat math does not apply counters |
| Life editor | set any seat's life total (1..=999) | public |

A sandbox life edit never ends the game: 0 or less is refused, because ending a
game is what a legal match does (CR 704.5a), not an override.

## 3. Legal match versus sandbox: the taint

The record is typed and durable:

* `SandboxRecord { edits: Vec<SandboxEdit> }` in `crates/core/src/sandbox.rs`,
  where each edit carries its kind, seat, turn, step and public description;
* the record is stored in `SessionSave.sandbox`, so it survives save/load;
* `SessionSave::validate` **refuses** a save that carries overrides but claims
  `sandbox_modified: false`, so clearing one boolean by hand cannot launder a
  sandbox game into a match result;
* every result surface uses the same sentence
  (`SandboxRecord::record_line`): *SANDBOX-MODIFIED — … this is NOT a legal
  match result (n sandbox override(s) [...])*. The header strip shows the same
  banner for the rest of the session, and a new game resets the record with the
  position;
* a tainted save is still loadable (the position is the player's), but its
  embedded replay is no longer certified and the UI never claims otherwise.

Legal-match actions are untouched: they stay in the persistent **YOUR ACTIONS**
strip, are validated by the engine's normal transactional path, and only the
engine's own legal-action generator can offer them.

## 4. Undo and study honesty

`Undo (U)` removes the most recent accepted action by **rebuilding** the
position from the deterministic recorded prefix (`Replay::branch_at` +
`run_recorded`), not by patching fields. Consequently:

* the RNG state, revision and decision serial are restored exactly, so replaying
  the same action from the restored position produces the identical digest;
* the log is rebuilt from the prefix, so nothing the undone action revealed (a
  draw, a scry look, a private choice) is still readable anywhere;
* undo is refused after a sandbox override, because the recorded line no longer
  produces the live position — silently substituting a different game would be
  dishonest. Start a new game or use **Return to branch** instead;
* undo replays the recorded prefix synchronously inside the frame (CPU only, no
  IO, no engine rule evaluation beyond the recorded actions), so a very long
  recorded line costs the first frame after the key press;
* `Set branch / Return to branch` (issue23) keeps its own snapshot semantics and
  hidden-information boundary message.

A study branch also replaces the live position and clears the taint record, so
the branch itself has to prove the replacement is the clean recorded prefix. It
does: a sandbox override bumps the engine revision and decision serial, so a cut
that reaches into anything recorded *after* an override fails the replay with
`stale submission` and the tainted session is left exactly as it was; a cut
*before* the override replays the recorded prefix to the same digest the table
had at that point, which is what makes clearing the taint honest rather than
cosmetic. Both halves are pinned by
`a_sandbox_taint_cannot_be_branched_into_a_clean_line`.

## 5. Destructive actions ask first

New game (`N`), Start new table, Load (`L`), Branch from replay (`G`), Reset
*sandbox* game and Start imported match all set a pending confirmation that is
rendered in the persistent primary strip. The question names the action, the
seed or the file, so it is never a generic "are you sure?". Both branch triggers
(the Study panel button and `G`) go through one helper, so the shortcut cannot
skip the question the button asks. `Cancel` and `Esc` change nothing, and a
failure (load/branch/import/table start) is shown in the error colour, never
swallowed. Nothing destructive runs on the first click.

## 6. Evidence and limits

* `crates/core/tests/issue20_sandbox.rs` — deterministic controls, masked scry
  look, refusals, save/load taint, laundry refusal, zone/search projection.
* `crates/ui/tests/issue20_controls.rs` — undo restores digest/RNG/decision
  serial and the same continuation; undo refused on a tainted line; taint
  survives save/load; pending-choice and empty-library refusals; a post-override
  branch refused while a pre-override cut replays the clean digest.
* `crates/ui/src/app.rs` (viewport + input tests) — the inspector is searchable
  and the sandbox panel reachable at 1280×720 *and* at the 1024×640 programmatic
  minimum, the taint banner is in the fixed strip, a destructive action waits for
  its confirmation, `G` asks the same branch question the panel button asks, and
  a failed table start / imported start is an error state rather than a hint.
* `evidence/issue20/DELIVERY.md` — the packaged-app journey actually walked.

Not claimed: arbitrary 100-card Commander or partners; counters as rules objects
(they are storage/display only); a model playing strength; release timing; a
legal match result for any sandbox game.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assert the recorded four-seat starter journey is exact and digest-verified.

Reads the artifacts produced by:
  aperture-cli selfplay --seed 1 --max-steps 12000 \
    --deck decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt (x4) \
    --commander-combat-practice --commander 0..3:Jasmine Boreal \
    --verbose --out ... --replay-out ...
"""

import collections
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
GAME = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.json"
REPLAY = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.replay.json"
LOG = ROOT / "evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.verbose.log"
DECK_TEXT = ROOT / "decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt"
SOURCED = ROOT / "fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json"


def variant(name):
    """CardId enum variant for a printed name (same rule as the catalog)."""
    return "".join(part.capitalize() for part in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", name))


def main():
    deck = collections.Counter()
    for line in DECK_TEXT.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("//"):
            continue
        quantity, name = line.split(" ", 1)
        deck[variant(name.strip())] += int(quantity)
    assert sum(deck.values()) == 99 and len(deck) == 60

    report = json.loads(GAME.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    replay = json.loads(REPLAY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    log = LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert report["status"] == "terminal", report["status"]
    assert report["starting_life"] == 40
    assert report["seat_count"] == 4
    assert report["pool_size"] == 79
    assert report["final_digest"] == replay["final_digest"]
    assert report["replay_digest_matches"] is True

    for seat, snapshot in enumerate(replay["seats"]):
        cards = collections.Counter()
        for card, quantity in snapshot["cards"]:
            cards[card] += quantity
        assert dict(cards) == dict(deck), f"seat {seat} library is not the exact list"
        assert sum(cards.values()) == 99

# Issue 17 — implementation handoff (slice 1, first starter package)

**Result: PARTIAL #17.** One supported starter is implemented, sourced,
analyzer-legal/supported and played as an exact four-seat 100-card snapshot.
The eight-list release gate remains open. No commit, push, PR, merge or issue
closure was performed.

* Branch: `aperture/issue-17`
* Base: `8a72cc607ea25f203be672c0007ad5e798be7145`
* Writer: ordinary OMP DeepSeek worker (not Vibe), sole writer
* Machine result: `evidence/issue17/implementation-result.json`
* TDD log: `evidence/issue17/TDD.md`

## Delivered package

`jasmine-vanilla-stompy`:

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| commander | **Jasmine Boreal** — `{3}{G}{W}`, Legendary Creature — Human, 4/5, printed rules text empty |
| library | **99 cards** in `decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt`; commander supplied separately |
| unique nonland cards | **58** (all singleton, all supported) |
| new sourced vanilla creatures | **47** |
| previously supported green/white nonland cards | 11 (4 vanilla creatures, 4 instants, 3 typed-ability creatures) |
| basic lands | **41** (20 Plains, 21 Forest) |
| total with commander | 100 |
| pool size | 31 → **79** (31 previous + 47 vanilla + Jasmine) |

No legendary library card, artifact/enchantment/snow creature, duplicate
nonbasic singleton, keyword, token, counter or unsupported text is used. The
unimplemented legend rule is not exercised outside the commander slot.

The commander registry is now the typed
`CardId::SUPPORTED_COMMANDERS = [IsamaruHoundOfKonda, JasmineBoreal]`; the
one-commander-per-seat and ordinary-library refusals are unchanged. No state
field, digest input, `RULES_REVISION`, replay version or save version changed.

## Source capture

All 61 referenced cards were fetched from Scryfall on **2026-10-25T07:59:45Z**:

* `GET https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=<name>` then
  `GET https://api.scryfall.com/cards/{set}/{collector_number}` for the returned
  concrete printing, paced at 120 ms.
* Raw responses, URLs and retrieval time:
  `evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json`.
* Per-card compact declaration:
  `fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json` (47 vanilla, 11 existing,
  2 basic lands, 1 commander; `role` is a local classification, all card fields
  are provider data).
* Kind `real` card snapshot and exact deck snapshot:
  `fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json` and
  `...deck.json`, with a fixture manifest binding `cards_sha256` and
  `deck_sha256`.
* Reproduction scripts: `evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py` and
  `evidence/issue17/generate-starter-fixtures.py`. A first re-run hit Scryfall
  HTTP 429; the successful capture at 07:59:45Z is the one recorded. No card
  metadata was invented.

A printing is not enough for support: every new card is also covered by
`crates/core/tests/starter_corpus.rs`, which asserts catalog name/cost/type/
power/toughness/empty rules **and** casts and resolves each of the 47 vanilla
creatures.

## Verification actually run

| gate | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focused tests | `cargo test -q -p aperture-core --test starter_corpus --test card_printings --test catalog_pool --test command_zone_setup --test practice_commander_guard --test issue13_commander_combat -p aperture-import --test starter_corpus_analyzer` | exit 0; log `evidence/issue17/focused-tests.log` |
| full suite | `cargo test -q --all-targets` | exit 0; **467 passed / 0 failed**, 71 suites, log `evidence/issue17/all-targets-tests.log` |
| fmt | `cargo fmt --all --check` | exit 0 |
| clippy | `cargo clippy -q --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| release CLI | `cargo build --release -p aperture-cli` | exit 0 |
| analyzer | `target/release/aperture-cli.exe commander-check --deck fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.deck.json --cards fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json --json` | exit 0; format `legal`, engine `supported`, 1 commander / 99 library / 100 total / 61 unique names, report `evidence/issue17/commander-check.json` |
| exact four-seat game | release `selfplay --seed 1 --max-steps 12000` with the starter file as all four `--deck` paths, `--commander-combat-practice`, and `--commander 0..3:"Jasmine Boreal"` | exit 0; **terminal**, winner P1, **2364 steps / 53 turns**, 40 starting life, digest `d7f8c2adaa17…`; 55 casts, 30 distinct new vanilla cards cast, 5 commander casts |
| separate replay | `target/release/aperture-cli.exe replay --file evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.replay.json` | exit 0; replayed digest matches recorded; log `evidence/issue17/replay-verify.log` |
| exact-list assertion | `python evidence/issue17/verify-starter-journey.py` | all four replay seats are exactly the 99-card list, all four commanders are Jasmine, digest matches; output `evidence/issue17/journey-verify.json` |

The game report is `evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.json`; the full event
log (including `P0..P3 casts Jasmine Boreal` and the vanilla casts) is
`evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.verbose.log`. A capped game would have
been reported as capped; this run is terminal.

`--help` was inspected from the release binary. `--commander` now documents both
explicit command-zone profiles and both supported commanders. Loading a deck
file now keeps the file's own name, so replay snapshots are not mislabeled as
"Temur Beats".

## Legacy preservation

No state/digest/version change was made, and the full suite's replay, save/load,
ordering and commander tests pass. A tracked issue-14 evidence replay
(`evidence/issue14-abilities-replay.json`, v6) fails to reproduce its recorded
digest; the **untouched base commit** fails identically with the same computed
and recorded digests. It predates issue-15 state fields and is not caused by
this change. All other tracked evidence replays are v1 and rejected by the
existing version policy. Details: `evidence/issue17/legacy-replay-note.md`.

## Corpus plan and gaps

`decks/starter-corpus/manifest.json` (version 1) lists all eight target ids and
commanders with statuses. `jasmine-vanilla-stompy` is `implemented` (not
`certified`); the other seven are `planned` with `deck_path: null`. No exact
future list is claimed. Six target commanders are not in the supported pool and
are named in each entry's `missing_cards`; interactions needed by the other
archetypes (tokens, triggered/activated abilities, keywords, counters, copying,
tribal payoffs, landfall, drain, sacrifice outlets) are listed in
`missing_interactions`. `docs/issue17-starter-corpus.md` explains the
archetypes, phased gaps and exclusion policy.

Remaining practical limits:

* The eight-list proof, per-card coverage for seven other styles, independent
  review and exact-head CI are still open; only one starter is playable.
* `isamaru-white-aggro` has its commander but no exact 99-card singleton library.
* The offline analyzer keeps its blanket `gameplay.available = false`; bounded
  command-zone/Commander-combat practice is still not the Commander format.
* The native UI's default startup table remains the practice decks; the starter
  is selected through explicit deck paths.
* The AI is the existing deterministic heuristic; no tuning was done.

## Coordinator-owned files

`.starter-run.yml` and `evidence/issue17/IMPLEMENT-1.md` were not edited.

A later `evidence/issue17/IMPLEMENT-2.md` appeared in the workspace during this
run. It was **not executed**: this admission bounded the run to slice 1 plus this
handoff, and the work order says to stop after implementation and handoff for
independent inspection. Its contents and other coordinator files were treated as
read-only.

The reporter pointer still targets completed m3-tabletop/#20. That discrepancy
was disclosed; no shared ops/reporting file was touched.

# Issue 17 — implementation handoff (slice 1, first starter package)

**Result: PARTIAL #17.** One supported starter is implemented, sourced,
analyzer-legal/supported and played as an exact four-seat 100-card snapshot.
The eight-list release gate remains open. No commit, push, PR, merge or issue
closure was performed.

* Branch: `aperture/issue-17`
* Base: `8a72cc607ea25f203be672c0007ad5e798be7145`
* Writer: ordinary OMP DeepSeek worker (not Vibe), sole writer
* Machine result: `evidence/issue17/implementation-result.json`
* TDD log: `evidence/issue17/TDD.md`

## Delivered package

`jasmine-vanilla-stompy`:

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| commander | **Jasmine Boreal** — `{3}{G}{W}`, Legendary Creature — Human, 4/5, printed rules text empty |
| library | **99 cards** in `decks/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.txt`; commander supplied separately |
| unique nonland cards | **58** (all singleton, all supported) |
| new sourced vanilla creatures | **47** |
| previously supported green/white nonland cards | 11 (4 vanilla creatures, 4 instants, 3 typed-ability creatures) |
| basic lands | **41** (20 Plains, 21 Forest) |
| total with commander | 100 |
| pool size | 31 → **79** (31 previous + 47 vanilla + Jasmine) |

No legendary library card, artifact/enchantment/snow creature, duplicate
nonbasic singleton, keyword, token, counter or unsupported text is used. The
unimplemented legend rule is not exercised outside the commander slot.

The commander registry is now the typed
`CardId::SUPPORTED_COMMANDERS = [IsamaruHoundOfKonda, JasmineBoreal]`; the
one-commander-per-seat and ordinary-library refusals are unchanged. No state
field, digest input, `RULES_REVISION`, replay version or save version changed.

## Source capture

All 61 referenced cards were fetched from Scryfall on **2026-10-25T07:59:45Z**:

* `GET https://api.scryfall.com/cards/named?exact=<name>` then
  `GET https://api.scryfall.com/cards/{set}/{collector_number}` for the returned
  concrete printing, paced at 120 ms.
* Raw responses, URLs and retrieval time:
  `evidence/issue17/scryfall-responses.json`.
* Per-card compact declaration:
  `fixtures/starter-corpus/sourced-cards.json` (47 vanilla, 11 existing,
  2 basic lands, 1 commander; `role` is a local classification, all card fields
  are provider data).
* Kind `real` card snapshot and exact deck snapshot:
  `fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json` and
  `...deck.json`, with a fixture manifest binding `cards_sha256` and
  `deck_sha256`.
* Reproduction scripts: `evidence/issue17/source-starter-cards.py` and
  `evidence/issue17/generate-starter-fixtures.py`. A first re-run hit Scryfall
  HTTP 429; the successful capture at 07:59:45Z is the one recorded. No card
  metadata was invented.

A printing is not enough for support: every new card is also covered by
`crates/core/tests/starter_corpus.rs`, which asserts catalog name/cost/type/
power/toughness/empty rules **and** casts and resolves each of the 47 vanilla
creatures.

## Verification actually run

| gate | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focused tests | `cargo test -q -p aperture-core --test starter_corpus --test card_printings --test catalog_pool --test command_zone_setup --test practice_commander_guard --test issue13_commander_combat -p aperture-import --test starter_corpus_analyzer` | exit 0; log `evidence/issue17/focused-tests.log` |
| full suite | `cargo test -q --all-targets` | exit 0; **467 passed / 0 failed**, 71 suites, log `evidence/issue17/all-targets-tests.log` |
| fmt | `cargo fmt --all --check` | exit 0 |
| clippy | `cargo clippy -q --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| release CLI | `cargo build --release -p aperture-cli` | exit 0 |
| analyzer | `target/release/aperture-cli.exe commander-check --deck fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.deck.json --cards fixtures/starter-corpus/jasmine-vanilla-stompy.cards.json --json` | exit 0; format `legal`, engine `supported`, 1 commander / 99 library / 100 total / 61 unique names, report `evidence/issue17/commander-check.json` |
| exact four-seat game | release `selfplay --seed 1 --max-steps 12000` with the starter file as all four `--deck` paths, `--commander-combat-practice`, and `--commander 0..3:"Jasmine Boreal"` | exit 0; **terminal**, winner P1, **2364 steps / 53 turns**, 40 starting life, digest `d7f8c2adaa17…`; 55 casts, 30 distinct new vanilla cards cast, 5 commander casts |
| separate replay | `target/release/aperture-cli.exe replay --file evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.replay.json` | exit 0; replayed digest matches recorded; log `evidence/issue17/replay-verify.log` |
| exact-list assertion | `python evidence/issue17/verify-starter-journey.py` | all four replay seats are exactly the 99-card list, all four commanders are Jasmine, digest matches; output `evidence/issue17/journey-verify.json` |

The game report is `evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.json`; the full event
log (including `P0..P3 casts Jasmine Boreal` and the vanilla casts) is
`evidence/issue17/jasmine-starter-game.verbose.log`. A capped game would have
been reported as capped; this run is terminal.

`--help` was inspected from the release binary. `--commander` now documents both
explicit command-zone profiles and both supported commanders. Loading a deck
file now keeps the file's own name, so replay snapshots are not mislabeled as
"Temur Beats".

## Legacy preservation

No state/digest/version change was made, and the full suite's replay, save/load,
ordering and commander tests pass. A tracked issue-14 evidence replay
(`evidence/issue14-abilities-replay.json`, v6) fails to reproduce its recorded
digest; the **untouched base commit** fails identically with the same computed
and recorded digests. It predates issue-15 state fields and is not caused by
this change. All other tracked evidence replays are v1 and rejected by the
existing version policy. Details: `evidence/issue17/legacy-replay-note.md`.

## Corpus plan and gaps

`decks/starter-corpus/manifest.json` (version 1) lists all eight target ids and
commanders with statuses. `jasmine-vanilla-stompy` is `implemented` (not
`certified`); the other seven are `planned` with `deck_path: null`. No exact
future list is claimed. Six target commanders are not in the supported pool and
are named in each entry's `missing_cards`; interactions needed by the other
archetypes (tokens, triggered/activated abilities, keywords, counters, copying,
tribal payoffs, landfall, drain, sacrifice outlets) are listed in
`missing_interactions`. `docs/issue17-starter-corpus.md` explains the
archetypes, phased gaps and exclusion policy.

Remaining practical limits:

* The eight-list proof, per-card coverage for seven other styles, independent
  review and exact-head CI are still open; only one starter is playable.
* `isamaru-white-aggro` has its commander but no exact 99-card singleton library.
* The offline analyzer keeps its blanket `gameplay.available = false`; bounded
  command-zone/Commander-combat practice is still not the Commander format.
* The native UI's default startup table remains the practice decks; the starter
  is selected through explicit deck paths.
* The AI is the existing deterministic heuristic; no tuning was done.

## Coordinator-owned files

`.starter-run.yml` and `evidence/issue17/IMPLEMENT-1.md` were not edited.

A later `evidence/issue17/IMPLEMENT-2.md` appeared in the workspace during this
run. It was **not executed**: this admission bounded the run to slice 1 plus this
handoff, and the work order says to stop after implementation and handoff for
independent inspection. Its contents and other coordinator files were treated as
read-only.

The reporter pointer still targets completed m3-tabletop/#20. That discrepancy
was disclosed; no shared ops/reporting file was touched.
